The upper southern shaft page: "From this point, all the way to the outlet on the pyramid’s flank (we measured both points), the shaft maintains an angle of 45°. So, despite the extreme fluctuations in the initial section, the shaft seem to proceed with great exactitude and constancy." It is the chord from the far end of Block No. 5 to the outlet, both ends measured, and so it is the angle claim C2’s ray should be drawn at; the 39.20° and 50.54° of Blocks 2 and 3 are the initial fluctuation and are carried separately as kc.shaft.south.segment.2.angle and .3.angle. Read on 2026-09-16 from the isida-project.org mirror named on this source, which carries the report's four shaft pages and its findings page in full.

The upper northern shaft page: "After the CAVIGLIA TUNNEL, from Block No. 6 on, the shaft continues in the usual form. The angle between this point and the point of the shaft’s outlet on the flank of the pyramid (we measured both points) is 32.60°." That settles the note this record used to carry: 32.60° is 32° 36′, so the report’s figure is the one stored and Bauval’s 32° 28′ is not it. The same page gives a second and different measurement, 31.20° averaged over five readings across the 11 m of the "Mankiller" tunnel, which is a local slope inside the run and is entered separately as kc.shaft.north.mankiller.angle. The lower southern shaft page: "After an initial horizontal section of 1.96 meters (penetrating the first block of the Queen’s Chamber wall), the shaft inclines at an average angle of 39.6078°, which we determined by taking 24 measurements over a distance of 28 meters." The four decimal places are the report’s own and are a mean of 24 readings, not a precision claim about any one of them. DECIDED 2026-09-16: kept at 39° 07′ as the value claim C2 is tested against, with the report’s measured spread as its sigma. The figure is widely quoted and attributed to the Upuaut survey, and it is the figure the shaft-and-star claim is stated with, so testing C2 against anything else would be testing a different claim. But the report’s text does not print it, so this record stays unverified. What the lower northern shaft page does say is: "Based on 14 measurements made over a distance of 17 meters, the shaft’s angle of ascent fluctuates between 33.3° and 40.1°", and of the intended angle, "Only further measurements in the still unexplored upper areas of the shaft will tell." The sigma of 3.4° is half that measured range, and 39° 07′ lies inside it. The bounds themselves are qc.shaft.north.angle.min and .max, both verified. Anyone reading C2’s Kochab residual of about fourteen arcminutes should read it against a shaft whose own measured slope wanders by nearly seven degrees.
